today.name: Resurf
today.tagline: A Personal Context Library for Mac
today.description: Resurf is a personal context app for things you like, care about, and work on. Save notes, links, images, PDFs, and ideas. Find them later or hand that context to AI through MCP and CLI. Native on Mac, iPhone, and iPad, with local storage and private iCloud sync.

comments.text: Hey guys, Deep here. I’m a design engineer and maker of Resurf.I save a lot of things while working. Inspiration, articles, screenshots, random ideas. They ended up scattered across apps, and I rarely came back to them. So I built Resurf for myself.It’s a personal context app for things you like, care about, and work on.Capture quickly: notes, links, PDFs, images, videos, and voice memos.Organize later: spaces, tags, and stacks. Search when you need something.Use that context with AI: ask your library inside Resurf, or hand it off to your AI tools through MCP and CLI.I’ve shared earlier versions on Reddit, and the feedback helped shape the app. It’s now fully native on Mac, iPhone, and iPad. Your library lives locally, with optional private iCloud sync.Free to try on Mac. Free on iPhone and iPad. One-time purchase for unlimited Mac use.Still polishing the small details. Would love to hear your thoughts and what you’d use it for 🙂
Love the idea of making a personal library useful context for AI! Can you limit MCP access to specific spaces or collections?
I gave it a try and its smooth. I was using obsidian for achieving same things. I'll post another review after 30 days, hoping for the best.
Wow! Looks cool! I often loose some files :)
Love that Resurf keeps everything local and private while still letting AI tap into your context through MCP and CLI, that balance of privacy and openness is genuinely rare.
Beautiful! Deserves a lot!

I use this app every single day, and couldn't go back. It permanently lives in my menu bar, and I store every single bit of inspiration I find! Whenever I'm designing anything, the first place I start is my Resurf library. Thanks for making this! 🙌🏻

مسئله و راه‌حل: کاربران و متخصصان روزانه با حجم عظیمی از داده‌ها، ایده‌ها و لینک‌ها مواجه هستند که معمولاً در ابزارهای مختلف پراکنده می‌شوند. Resurf با ارائه یک کتابخانه شخصی زمینه (Context Library) محلی، امکان ذخیره سریع انواع محتوا و تغذیه آن‌ها به ابزارهای هوش مصنوعی از طریق پروتکل‌های استاندارد مانند MCP را فراهم می‌کند.

معماری و تکنولوژی: استفاده از اپلیکیشن‌های نیتیو (Native) روی اکوسیستم اپل با ذخیره‌سازی محلی و همگام‌سازی خصوصی iCloud، امنیت و سرعت بالایی ایجاد کرده است. ارائه رابط‌های MCP (Model Context Protocol) و CLI امکان یکپارچه‌سازی بی‌دردسر با عامل‌های هوش مصنوعی (AI Agents) را مهیا می‌سازد.

مدل درآمدی: مدل فری‌میوم (Freemium) ترکیبی شامل نسخه رایگان روی موبایل و خرید یک‌باره (One-time purchase) برای دسکتاپ (مک)، که برای کاربران ابزارهای کاربردی بسیار جذاب است.

نقاط قوت: حفظ کامل حریم خصوصی با ذخیره‌سازی محلی، اتصال مستقیم به هوش مصنوعی با MCP، سرعت بالای نرم‌افزار نیتیو، و رابط کاربری ساده در منوبار.

نقاط ضعف: محدود بودن به اکوسیستم اپل در حال حاضر و نیاز به دانش نسبی هوش مصنوعی برای بهره‌برداری کامل از ویژگی‌های MCP.

نکته طلایی برای ایران: در بازار ایران، ارائه نسخه دسکتاپ چندسکویی (با Tauri یا Electron) متصل به مدل‌های زبانی بزرگ بومی یا APIهای هوش مصنوعی بدون تحریم، همراه با پشتیبانی کامل از راست‌چین و زبان فارسی می‌تواند این ابزار را به اصلی‌ترین مرکز مدیریت دانش (PKM) برنامه‌نویسان و طراحان ایرانی تبدیل کند.

today.name: Perplexity Hybrid Compute
today.tagline: Splitting AI tasks: Cloud for research, Mac for privacy
today.description: Hybrid Compute is now live on Perplexity Computer, their Mac app. It splits a task between the cloud and your own Mac: research and reasoning happen in the cloud with their strongest AI, while anything touching your private files stays on your Mac with a local AI, so it never gets uploaded. Works on Apple silicon, 24GB RAM minimum, live now for Pro/Max/Enterprise.

comments.text: Hybrid Compute is now live on Perplexity Computer, splitting a task between the cloud and your own Mac.Problem: AI tools that work with your private files usually mean choosing between power and privacy. Cloud AI is smarter but means uploading sensitive stuff. Local AI keeps things private but is weaker.Solution: One task now runs in two places. Research and reasoning happen in the cloud with their strongest AI. Anything touching your private files, like client documents or sensitive numbers, stays on your Mac and gets handled by a local AI, so it never gets uploaded.Key features:Cloud AI for research and reasoning, local AI for private filesOn-device privacy checker that masks, blocks, or asks before anything sensitive leaves your MacTrigger tasks remotely from iPhone, sensitive steps still run on your Mac3 local models to choose from, one-click setup, no Ollama or API key neededEnterprise admin controls and audit logs for what leaves a deviceWho it's for: Anyone working with sensitive data alongside AI who doesn't want private files touching the cloud.Try it at https://www.perplexity.ai/hub/products/hybrid-compute P.S. today.name: Cognition's SWE-2
today.tagline: Cognition's coding model, 64% cheaper than Fable 5.1
today.description: SWE-2 is Cognition's new coding model, post-trained from Kimi K3 with RL that optimizes for cost and capability at the same time. It hits 50.0% on FrontierCode 1.1 Main, within a point of Fable 5.1 at 64% less, and lands within a few points of GPT-6 Astra at a quarter of the cost. Compared to SWE-1.7 it takes 58% fewer turns and costs 81% less while scoring higher. Available now in Devin Desktop and CLI.

comments.text: SWE-2 is Cognition's new coding model, built to sit near the frontier without frontier pricing.The problem: coding agents get smarter by getting more expensive, and often by burning tokens. Their own SWE-1.7 had this issue, users said it over-explored simple tasks.What they did: post-trained Kimi K3 with RL that puts the actual dollar cost of a run into the training reward, and trains all three effort levels (medium, high, max) in one go instead of stitching separate models together. So the whole cost-performance curve moves up, not just the top end.The numbers:50.0% on FrontierCode 1.1 Main, within a point of Fable 5.1 at 64% less costWithin a few points of GPT-6 Astra at a quarter of the price92.8% on Terminal-Bench 2.1, top of their comparison tablevs SWE-1.7: 58% fewer turns, 81% cheaper, higher score. First code edit after 18 steps instead of 48Also worth noting: better end-to-end test writing, and it re-derives conclusions when you push back instead of just agreeing with you.Good fit if you're running coding agents at volume and per-task cost is an actual line item. comments.text: Hi Product Hunt 👋 I'm a solo developer, and I built Clipwise because every Notion web clipper I tried wanted me to create an account and log in — and those logins kept breaking or syncing slowly, right when I just wanted to save something quickly. Clipwise takes that whole layer out. You connect it once with your own Notion integration (a single paste), and after that it just works. No account with me, no server, nothing leaves your computer except the page you choose to save — which goes straight to your own Notion. A few things I cared about: • It saves the whole article, not half of it — including code blocks and content some clippers miss. • You fill in your Notion properties (tags, status, source…) before saving, so the page lands finished instead of as an empty row. • It remembers your last database, so the second clip is basically one click. • If a page comes out empty, it tells you instead of silently saving nothing. comments.text: Hey Product Hunt! I’m Gustav, one of the makers of Epilude. Epilude started as a way to write with my voice after I hurt my elbow. Today, we’re launching Notetaker. It's the next step in helping you spend less time typing and more time thinking. I’ve always found meetings slightly self-defeating: either I focus on the conversation and forget half of what was agreed, or I take detailed notes and miss the conversation happening in front of me. Existing AI notetakers solve that problem, but they all send your data to cloud providers such as Anthropic and OpenAI, where you risk your data becoming part of their training data. We wanted something more private. Notetaker transcribes and summarises your meetings all locally on your Mac using our in-house trained model EP-1. That way, none of your data leaves your Mac, and your notes remain yours. When the meeting ends, Epilude gives you a clean transcript, an editable summary, and action items with owners and due dates. It automatically adapts the notes to the kind of meeting you had, so a standup, sales call, and planning session don’t all come back in the same generic format. Every key point links back to the transcript, making it easy to check exactly what was said. Each meeting is also saved as a Markdown file in a folder on your Mac, so you can open it in Obsidian, paste it into Notion, export it as a PDF, or keep it wherever you already work. Epilude Notetaker records directly from your Mac, so no bot joins the call and there’s nothing to invite or connect. If your Mac can hear the meeting, Epilude can take the notes, whether you’re using Zoom, Google Meet, Teams, Slack, or talking across a table. My favourite part is simply being more present. I can stop half-listening while trying to write everything down and trust that the decisions and follow-ups will still be there when the call ends. Epilude is Mac-only for now. We’d love to hear what you think. Try it on your next call and let us know what we missed! You can try it (as well as our completely local dictation) for free.

Double-tap Left Ctrl in any text field, in any app, and the reply is there — drawn from the thread on screen, your calendar, your files and your past meetings, indexed in an encrypted vault on your PC. It won't double-book you, and it matches how you write to that person, down to the sign-off. Then it stops: it types into the box and never sends. Windows.

comments.text: Hey Product Hunt 👋I'm Tery. I've been shipping software for 40 years, since a Tandy CoCo with 4K of RAM. In 1999 it annoyed me that Pocket PC shipped without Access, so I built one — abcDB stayed the #1 Pocket PC database for a decade, across 135 countries. Even the UN ran it.That was trick one. Very excited to present another 🚀MyHandler is a local-first AI for Windows — think OpenClaw, for the rest of us who don't have a Mac Mini in a closet. It indexes your screen, files, mail, dictations, calendar and meetings into an encrypted vault on your own drive. Not our servers.✍️ Ghostwriter is the feature I'd start with.If you've ever sat staring at a blinking cursor, this is for you.Double-tap Left Ctrl in any text field, in any app.It reads what's on screen and works out what you were about to write.You get a draft in your voice ... pulling from your calendar, files and past meetings.Where OpenClaw acts for you, Ghostwriter never sends. yesterday.name: QApilot MCP for Android
yesterday.tagline: Android app testing inside your coding agent
yesterday.description: QApilot MCP automates tests on real Android devices and emulators by talking to Claude, Cursor or Codex. Describe a test flow in plain English, no Appium code required. Your agent lays out the steps. QApilot runs the steps. It finds the elements, waits for the screen to settle, retries when something moves, and caches what it learns so repeat runs are faster. Every pass saves a Gherkin feature file and becomes a replayable test case. Needs Node, Java and the Android SDK.

comments.text: Hey Product Hunt!I am Charan. Thrilled to bring QApilot MCP to you. → https://qapilot.io/mcp/guideAndroid app testing inside your AI client. You describe what needs to hold in plain English, and it runs on a device or emulator connected to your machine.The specifics:Android only. iOS is next.Native Android apps. Hybrid and WebView aren't supported yet.Local device or emulator.Tested configs for Claude Desktop, Cursor and Codex.You'll need Node, Java, the Android SDK, and Appium running locally.Why an MCP?Coding agents made mobile code cheap to write. They did nothing for verifying it, so the bottleneck just moved. A mobile lead put it well: "by the time your report reaches me, I've merged three more PRs." Our testing wasn't wrong. It was happening too late, in a tool he never opened. MCP is how we moved it into his editor.What it doesYou tell your agent what needs to hold: "verify checkout still works after this refactor." It lays out the steps; QApilot finds the actual element behind "Checkout" on a real Android screen, waits for it to settle, retries when something moves, and says so honestly when it can't.You get a verdict, a live browser preview, and files on disk: YAML, JSON steps, Gherkin on pass. Accept a run and it becomes a test case you can replay by ID, in batch, or from Excel. It caches what it learns per app, so it gets faster the more you use it.The part we care most aboutIt runs on your machine. Your app, your screenshots and your runs don't get uploaded. Only your account and the test cases you explicitly save go to QApilot. Most tools here force every run through their cloud behind a tunnel, and for a lot of teams that's an immediate no. We didn't want to build that.If you build Android apps with a coding agent, I'd like to know what you still check by hand before every merge. That's what shapes where this goes next.Happy to answer anything in the comments.

comments.text: Hi Product Hunt, I made Kabza. Pick Noida, Delhi, Gurugram or Bengaluru. Start with one territory. Your supporters grow over time, and each drag sends half of them to another territory. Send more than its defenders and it becomes yours. The fun is choosing when to push and when to hold back. yesterday.name: DockFix 5.0
yesterday.tagline: Replace the macOS Dock with one that is truly yours.
yesterday.description: Replace the macOS Dock with one that is truly yours. Custom colors, icons and animations, plus widgets, window previews and a file shelf.
yesterday.category: Productivity • User Experience • Menu Bar Apps
yesterday.categoryFa: بهره‌وری • User Experience • Menu Bar Apps

comments.text: DockFix exists for one reason. The Dock that comes with your Mac is not yours. Apple designed it to be fast and reliable, and then closed it: you cannot personalize its colour, its icons, its animations, or much of what sits inside it. We built DockFix to hand all of that back to you. What we have always been after is harder than it sounds. A dock you have made your own is only worth having if it still feels like part of macOS. The magnification has to carry the right weight. A window has to fold toward the corner it came from. An icon has to appear the instant the app does. Miss any of that and people feel it straight away, even when they could not tell you what is wrong. So this year we stopped adding to what we had and rebuilt the app from nothing. A new engine, a new interface, and not one line of the old code left in place. It took months, and nothing else shipped while it was happening, because a rewrite is not something you can do halfway. What came out of it is the DockFix I wanted to make in the first place. It looks and moves like the dock Apple ships, and then it does what Apple’s will not: window previews, widgets, custom icons, folders, presets, the file shelf. None of it feels bolted on, because none of it is. It is available now, and free if you already own DockFix. I would like you to see it for yourself.
What happens to the layout when an external display disconnects? Mine reshuffles every time I undock and I put it back by hand.

I am a huge fan of macOS extensions and use BoringNotch and some other stuff. DockFix concept is pretty neat; I like the idea of widgets inside the dock, although the setup is a bit frustrating. But the overall idea is great. Good luck with your launch!

yesterday.faDescription: داک مک‌او‌اس خود را با داکی جایگزین کنید که واقعاً متعلق به شماست. این نرم‌افزار امکان شخصی‌سازی کامل رنگ‌ها، آیکون‌ها و پویانمایی‌های داک را برای شما فراهم می‌سازد. علاوه بر این، ویژگی‌های قدرتمندی مانند ویجت‌های کاربردی داخل داک، پیش‌نمایش زنده پنجره‌ها و شلف نگهداری فایل‌ها را در اختیارتان قرار می‌دهد. با استفاده از این ابزار می‌توانید تجربه کاربری مک‌او‌اس را دقیقاً مطابق با نیازها و سلیقه شخصی خود بازآفرینی کنید.

faComments.text: داک‌فیکس فقط به یک دلیل وجود دارد: داکی که همراه مک شما عرضه می‌شود، واقعاً متعلق به شما نیست. اپل آن را طوری طراحی کرده که سریع و قابل اعتماد باشد، اما آن را کاملاً بسته نگه داشته است؛ شما نمی‌توانید رنگ، آیکون‌ها، پویانمایی‌ها یا بخش زیادی از محتوای آن را شخصی‌سازی کنید. ما داک‌فیکس را ساختیم تا همه این امکانات را به شما بازگردانیم. آنچه همواره دنبالش بوده‌ایم سخت‌تر از چیزی است که به نظر می‌رسد؛ داکی که به سلیقه خود ساخته‌اید تنها زمانی ارزش دارد که همچنان حس بخشی از مک‌او‌اس را منتقل کند. بزرگ‌نمایی باید وزن مناسبی داشته باشد، پنجره باید به سمتی که از آن آمده تا شود و آیکون باید بلافاصله پس از اجرای برنامه ظاهر گردد. اگر هرکدام از این موارد رعایت نشود، کاربران فوراً آن را حس می‌کنند، حتی اگر نتوانند بگویند مشکل دقیقاً چیست. بنابراین امسال افزودن ویژگی‌های جدید را متوقف کردیم و برنامه را از صفر بازسازی نمودیم. یک موتور جدید، یک رابط کاربری جدید و بدون استفاده از حتی یک خط از کد قدیمی. این کار چند ماه طول کشید و در این مدت هیچ به‌روزرسانی دیگری منتشر نشد، چرا که بازنویسی کدهای یک نرم‌افزار را نمی‌توان نیمه‌کاره انجام داد. نتیجه آن همان داک‌فیکسی شد که از ابتدا می‌خواستم بسازم. این نسخه ظاهر و حرکتی کاملاً شبیه به داک اصلی اپل دارد و در عین حال کارهایی را انجام می‌دهد که داک اپل قادر به انجامشان نیست: پیش‌نمایش پنجره‌ها، ویجت‌ها، آیکون‌های اختصاصی، پوشه‌ها، تنظیمات پیش‌فرض و شلف فایل‌ها. هیچ‌کدام از این بخش‌ها وصله ناچسب به نظر نمی‌رسند زیرا واقعاً این‌طور نیستند. این نسخه هم‌اکنون در دسترس است و برای کسانی که قبلاً داک‌فیکس را خریده‌اند کاملاً رایگان خواهد بود. دوست دارم خودتان آن را امتحان کنید.
وقتی نمایشگر خارجی قطع می‌شود چه اتفاقی برای چیدمان می‌افتد؟ چیدمان داک من هر بار که مک‌بوک را از داک‌پایه جدا می‌کنم به هم می‌ریزد و مجبورم آن را دستی مرتب کنم.

من از طرفداران سرسخت افزونه‌های مک‌او‌اس هستم و از BoringNotch و چند ابزار دیگر استفاده می‌کنم. ایده داک‌فیکس بسیار جذاب است؛ ایده قرارگیری ویجت‌ها داخل داک را دوست دارم، اگرچه راه‌اندازی اولیه آن کمی گیج‌کننده است. اما در کل ایده فوق‌العاده‌ای است. در انتشار محصولتان موفق باشید!

yesterday.name: Wokyintosh
yesterday.tagline: Turn a spare Mac display into a retro system dashboard!
yesterday.description: Wokyintosh is a free, open-source macOS dashboard inspired by the classic Macintosh. It combines a large clock and date, local weather, Apple Music and Spotify Now Playing with artwork, plus live CPU, RAM, SSD and network stats. I built it for my Wokyis M5 Retro Dock Station after months of not finding the dashboard I wanted — even among paid apps.

comments.text: Hey Product Hunt! 👋 Wokyintosh started with a very specific frustration. I bought a Wokyis M5 Retro Dock Station for my Mac mini and really liked the hardware, but after several months I still couldn't find the dashboard I wanted for its little display — not even a paid one. I wanted something simple: a huge clock and date, weather, Apple Music / Spotify Now Playing, artwork, and a few useful system stats, all with a classic Macintosh feel. So I decided to build it myself. I'm not an experienced macOS developer, so I used ChatGPT as part of a vibe-coding workflow and learned, tested and debugged the app as I went. Wokyintosh 1.0 is now free and open source. I'd especially love feedback on what you'd want in a future settings panel, layout customization, and better support for small secondary displays. Thanks for checking it out!
Could this work nicely on an older Mac that isn't powerful enough for everyday use but still has a good display?

You asked for settings panel feedback, so the one I'd put above layout customization is idle cost. An always on dashboard that repaints the clock every frame keeps the GPU awake, and on a Mac mini nobody notices, but whoever runs this on a laptop's second display uninstalls it inside a week. Repainting once a second, and only when a value actually changed, is boring and it's the whole difference. Also the part I find more interesting than the retro look is that you vibe-coded a macOS app and then actually opened the repo, because the usual version of that story ends at the screenshot.
I like that it supports both Apple Music and Spotify. That makes it much more practical for different setups.
The retro Mac-style look is a fun touch. It gives an old spare display a purpose instead of just letting it sit unused.

### مسئله و راه‌حل
محصول Wokyintosh به عنوان یک داشبورد نوستالژیک برای macOS، مشکل عدم وجود برنامه‌های ساده، زیبا و کم‌حجم برای نمایشگرهای دوم یا جانبی (مانند داک‌های رترو) را حل می‌کند. این نرم‌افزار اطلاعات حیاتی مانند ساعت، آب‌وهوا، وضعیت سیستم (CPU، RAM، شبکه) و موزیک در حال پخش را در قالب یک واژه‌پرداز یا سیستم‌عامل مک کلاسیک ادغام کرده و به نمایشگرهای بلااستفاده هویت جدیدی می‌بخشد.

### معماری و تکنولوژی
ویژگی منحصربه‌فرد این پروژه توسعه آن از طریق متدولوژی Vibe Coding با کمک چت‌جی‌پتی توسط یک توسعه‌دهنده غیرحرفه‌ای macOS است. نرم‌افزار به صورت اپلیکیشن نیتیو macOS با استفاده از APIهای سیستم برای خواندن داده‌های سخت‌افزاری و ادغام با Apple Music و Spotify پیاده‌سازی شده و سورس‌کد آن به صورت رایگان و open-source منتشر گردیده است.

### مدل درآمدی
پروژه در حال حاضر کاملاً رایگان و open-source است، اما قابلیت‌های تجاری‌سازی آینده شامل فروش تم‌ها و قالب‌های سفارشی، عرضه نسخه پرمیوم با امکانات شخصی‌سازی پیشرفته چیدمان، یا همکاری با سازندگان سخت‌افزارهای جانبی (مانند Wokyis) برای عرضه به عنوان نرم‌افزار پیش‌فرض می‌باشد.

### نقاط قوت
- طراحی نوستالژیک و بسیار جذاب برای علاقه‌مندان به طراحی رترو
- پشتیبانی هم‌زمان از اپل موزیک و اسپاتیفای
- رایگان و open-source بودن که موجب جلب اعتماد جامعه توسعه‌دهندگان می‌شود
- کاربردی کردن مانیتورهای قدیمی و ثانویه

### نقاط ضعف
- محدود بودن به اکوسیستم macOS در حال حاضر
- عدم بهینه‌سازی دقیق رندرینگ فریم‌ها که می‌تواند منجر به مصرف غیرضروری GPU در حالت بی‌کاری شود
- نبود پنل تنظیمات جامع در نسخه اولیه (v۱.۰)

### نکته طلایی برای ایران
برای موفقیت مشابه در بازار ایران، می‌توان پروژه‌ای چندپلتفرمی (مثلاً با Tauri) توسعه داد که روی تبلت‌های قدیمی اندرویدی/آی‌پد یا مانیتورهای کوچک کار کند. افزودن ویژگی‌های بومی مثل تقویم شمسی و اوقات شرعی، نمایش نرخ لحظه‌ای ارز/طلا، و اتصال به پادکست‌خوان‌ها و پخش‌کننده‌های ایرانی، این ابزار را به یک اکسسوری ضروری و محبوب برای میز کار فریلنسرها و مهندسان نرم‌افزار در ایران تبدیل خواهد کرد.

yesterday.name: Stackness
yesterday.tagline: Show your stack! The social home for your dev tools
yesterday.description: Stackness is where developers and vibe coders show the tools, workflows, and approaches they build with. Build a stack profile you share as one link, post your moves, follow people whose taste you trust, and watch tools rise and fall. Free and with an MCP server.

comments.text: Hey everyone, I'm very happy to share that I've launched a first version of the Stackness platform. It's a social platform where people can share how they build software and the tools and techniques they use. You can also see which tools and workflows are popular right now. My main goal is to have a community that can share, discuss, and discover new things in the tech world. I would really appreciate it if you could let me know whether it's relevant to you and what do you think about the platform in general :)
Will there be a way to compare two people’s stacks and quickly see which tools they have in common?
The idea of following people based on their tool choices is interesting. Sometimes you find better tools through somenes workflow than through a search.
Can you update your stack whenever you switch tools and does the shared link update automatically?
I like the social side of this. Seeing what tools other developers actually use can be more useful than reading endless tool list.
The one link stack profile is a really handy idea. It would be nice to share your whole setup without having to list every tool separately.

You asked whether it's relevant. The thing that kills every stack profile site is staleness, because mine would be accurate for about three weeks and then sit there lying about a tool I dropped, and I'm not coming back to edit it. The MCP server is the most interesting thing here and it's the last four words of your description, since that's the one path where the profile updates itself instead of nagging me. I'd make reading a repo or a package file the default way a stack gets built and leave manual entry as the fallback.

yesterday.faDescription: استکنِس (Stackness) پلتفرمی است که توسعه‌دهندگان و برنامه‌نویسان در آن ابزارها، گردش‌های کاری و روش‌های ساخت نرم‌افزار خود را به اشتراک می‌گذارند. شما می‌توانید یک پروفایل اختصاصی از مجموعه‌ابزارهای (Stack) خود بسازید و آن را تنها در قالب یک لینک واحد منتشر کنید. در این شبکه اجتماعی امکان اشتراک‌گذاری تغییرات، دنبال کردن افراد مورد اعتماد و رصد صعود یا افول ابزارهای مختلف وجود دارد. این سرویس به صورت رایگان و همراه با سرور MCP ارائه می‌شود تا تجربه کاربری هوشمند و به‌روزرسانی آسانی را رقم بزند.

yesterday.aiReview:
مسئله و راه‌حل: توسعه‌دهندگان همواره علاقه‌مند به آگاهی از ابزارها و روش‌های کاری یکدیگر هستند، اما اشتراک‌گذاری این اطلاعات معمولاً پراکنده و دستی است. Stackness با ارائه یک پروفایل تک‌لینکی و شبکه اجتماعی تخصصی، امکان به اشتراک‌گذاری و رصد ابزارهای محبوب را فراهم می‌سازد.

معماری و تکنولوژی: استفاده از پروتکل MCP (Model Context Protocol) نقطه عطف معمارانه این ابزار است که امکان همگام‌سازی خودکار استک از طریق هوش مصنوعی و فایل‌های پروژه‌ای را فراهم می‌کند. فرانت‌اند مبتنی بر وب سریع و سبک با قابلیت ساخت آسان لینک‌های اشتراک‌گذاری طراحی شده است.

مدل درآمدی: مدل فری‌میوم (Freemium) با امکان ارائه خدمات ویژه برای تیم‌ها و شرکت‌ها جهت نمایش استک سازمانی، به همراه فرصت‌های تبلیغاتی اسپانسری برای ابزارهای نوظهور.

نقاط قوت: سادگی اشتراک‌گذاری (تک‌لینک)، بهره‌گیری از جذابیت‌های شبکه اجتماعی و به‌روزرسانی خودکار هوشمند با MCP.

نقاط ضعف: خطر بالای کهنه شدن داده‌ها در صورت عدم استفاده از به‌روزرسانی خودکار و وابستگی شدید به ایجاد اثر شبکه‌ای (Network Effect).

نکته طلایی برای ایران: برای موفقیت نسخه ایرانی، اتصال مستقیم به مخازن گیت‌هاب/گیت‌لب کاربران برای استخراج خودکار استک فنی پروژه‌ها الزامی است؛ همچنین ایجاد بخش «برند کارفرمایی» برای شرکت‌های ایرانی جهت نمایش فناوری‌های مورد استفاده‌شان می‌تواند منبع درآمدی بسیار پایدار و جذابی باشد.

iranEquivalent.description: پلتفرم بومی «استک‌باز» شبکه اجتماعی تخصصی توسعه‌دهندگان ایرانی برای معرفی ابزارها و فرآیندهای توسعه نرم‌افزار است. این ابزار به برنامه‌نویسان امکان می‌دهد استک فنی خود را در قالب یک لینک رزومه متمرکز کنند. همچنین قابلیت همگام‌سازی خودکار با پروژه‌های گیت‌هاب را برای جلوگیری از قدیمی شدن اطلاعات ارائه می‌دهد.

week.name: Switch
week.tagline: Bring any AI agent into Slack, Teams & Discord
week.description: Switch brings AI agents into the collaboration tools your team already uses. Agents join as named participants in your Slack, Teams, Discord, or Telegram channels, sharing the same context and history as your team. Connect an agent once and use it across projects. Each room carries its own context, participants, and rules. Works with Claude Code, OpenAI, Google ADK, LangChain, and more. Open source, self-hostable, running in minutes.
week.category: Open Source • Developer Tools • Artificial Intelligence

week.name: Anysite.io
week.tagline: Build and enrich B2B lists by chatting to your agent
week.description: Anysite.io is a B2B data layer living in your favorite AI agent. Ask your agent for the list you need — companies by geo, industry, and size; the people inside them; their current job titles and emails — and Anysite.io returns it. No queries to write, no scrapers to maintain. Works over MCP or REST API inside Claude, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, and other agents. Plug in and launch your outbound data collection the same day.

week.name: Harden
week.tagline: A security layer for AI coding agents
week.description: Harden AIF is a free, local security tool for AI coding agents. Its post-trained model checks tool calls before they run, using your request and session context. It beat frontier models on key agent-security benchmarks, while keeping your repo and tool output on your machine.

week.name: Loqua
week.tagline: Speak naturally and move from thoughts to being done
week.description: Your thoughts shouldn’t have to slow down for a keyboard. With Loqua, you can speak naturally to turn rough ideas into ready-to-use writing, understand what’s on your screen, listen when you’d rather not read, and move work forward by voice - from rewriting and translation to scheduling and coding workflows. month.name: PaymentKit
month.tagline: Billing that survives a processor shutdown
month.description: PaymentKit is a multi-processor billing platform for SaaS and e-commerce. It routes payments across processors, vaults tokens independently, and keeps subscriptions billing even if a MID gets shut down. No code to launch, full API when you need it.

comments.text: Hey everyone, Diego here from the PaymentKit team.Quick story on where this came from, because it explains most of the product.PaymentKit didn't start as a startup idea. We built it for ourselves. Our parent company runs a portfolio of subscription brands, and for years we kept hitting the same three problems: billing lived in one tool, payments in another, and revenue data in a third. Every processor change meant a migration. Every decline was money we never saw again. And all of it sat on top of a single processor whose risk team could change our business overnight.We couldn't find anything that solved all three together, so we built it and ran our own volume through it before selling it to anyone.What it actually does:Payment orchestration: Connect the processors you already use. Every transaction routes to the one most likely to approve it, and soft declines cascade to the next one automatically instead of turning into lost revenue.Independent vaulting: The part we care most about. Cards, Apple Pay and Google Pay are all vaulted as network tokens under your control, not your processor's. You can add or drop a processor without asking a single customer to re enter anything, and if a MID gets shut down your subscribers never feel it.Subscription billing: Flat, tiered, usage based or hybrid pricing. Hosted checkout and self service portals, live without writing code.Revenue metrics: One dashboard across every processor, so you can compare success rates and fees side by side instead of stitching exports together.What that actually produces: More than 10% lift in authorization rates on average after merchants switch. It comes from three things stacked: routing each transaction to the processor most likely to approve it, cascading soft declines instead of eating them, and network tokens that keep cards on file alive longer. One merchant went from 63% to 76%. There's also a risk side that most people only learn the hard way. Visa dropped the excessive VAMP threshold from 2.20% to 1.50% on April 1st this year across the US, Canada, Europe and Asia Pacific, and the ratio is measured per MID, not per company. If all your volume sits in one account, one bad month becomes a company level problem. Running multiple processors means you see the ratio per MID instead of hearing about it from your acquirer after the fact, and you can rebalance volume before any single account gets near the line.Why I think this community in particular might care: a lot of you are running SaaS or digital products on a single processor, or on a merchant of record that owns your customer data and your tokens. That works right up until it doesn't. We're the layer that makes that decision reversible.It goes live in under an hour on top of what you already have, and there's a free trial if you want to poke at it.Would really like to hear from anyone who's been through a processor shutdown, a rolling reserve, or a migration that broke their subscriptions. What did you wish existed at that moment?

@diego_vidal10 Congrats on the launch, and very cool product! Full disclosure — I'm a big fan of Anthropic and actually built an app that works exclusively with Claude Desktop for secure local file search. So I've spent a lot of time thinking about this space.My concern with Cowork isn't the vision, it's the architecture. Agentic tasks burn through tokens fast (Anthropic says so themselves), so that $200/month cap can disappear quicker than you'd expect. And at that price, you'd want to use it for real work — but the whole thing requires giving Claude direct read/write/delete access to your files. If you're handling client data, patient records, or anything regulated, you're basically out.The bigger issue is prompt injection. Anthropic admits "the chances of an attack are still non-zero" — and back in October 2025, researchers showed exactly that: a prompt injection against Claude that pulled up to 30MB of user data per request through Anthropic's own API. When you're talking about an agent with file system access, email connectors, and a browser, that's not some theoretical edge case.There's a reason some of us build tools where Claude can search your files without actually touching them. The agentic future is definitely coming, but "AI that can access everything" and "AI that keeps you in control" are two very different products for two very different users.

comments.text: Hey Product Hunt 👋 Joel here, one of the two Swedish founders building Goldfish.Why we built it:We started building Goldfish because AI still has one weird problem: it knows the internet, but not the work sitting right in front of you. AI has memory like a goldfish!Your messages, docs, tabs, meetings, half-written drafts, people, decisions, and loose threads already live on your computer. You paste the thread, explain the project, describe the person, and try to make it sound like you.That felt backwards to us.What Goldfish is:Goldfish is a private AI memory layer for your Mac. Something that understands your context privately, shows up where you already are, and removes the need to re-explain yourself 50 times a day.Early traction:We’ve worked closely with 1,000+ founding members to build a product people can’t live without.
